title: 'May be jailed, but I’ll return to Bangladesh this December,' says Sheikh Hasina
content: Sheikh Hasina declared she is not afraid of arrest upon her return to Bangladesh in December. She stated her return is for the nation's future and to set it on the right track. Dhaka reacted sharply, calling her an absconding convicted genocider and expressing regret over the event. Hasina described the July Uprising as a regime change operation orchestrated by a mastermind.

title: Meta apologises for ‘error in restricting PM’s video’
content: Meta's CEO Mark Zuckerberg formally apologized to the Indian government over several operational missteps, including issues with paid content amplification. The acknowledgment of these errors comes as officials expressed concerns over the potential loss of safe harbor protection for the platform. As the government reassesses its child online safety regulations, Meta committed to implementing necessary corrective actions to address these concerns.

title: Deal on Hormuz shipping route reached with Oman, says Iran
content: Iran and Oman have agreed on a proposed shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz. This agreement is a potential step toward reopening the critical waterway for energy supplies. A joint statement from Tehran and Muscat is currently in the final drafting stage. Sources indicate Iran would gain control over ships entering the Gulf via the strait. Talks continue, but finalization depends on third-party non-obstruction and detailed definitions.

title: 'Respect senior players': Rahane warns Gambhir amid India's Test struggles
content: Rahane also pointed to the rapid transition in the Indian Test side. Within six months, India lost Ravichandran Ashwin, Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli from the Test setup. Without naming anyone directly, he said a Test team needs more experienced players alongside youngsters.

title: Ex-Ethiopian Air chief Tewolde Gebremariam becomes Air India CEO
content: Air India has appointed Tewolde Gebremariam as its new CEO and MD. He previously led Ethiopian Airlines for over 36 years, achieving significant growth. Gebremariam will succeed Campbell Wilson, who stabilized the airline initially. The Tata Group aims for profitable expansion and operational excellence under his leadership. Gebremariam expressed excitement about building a world-class global airline for India.

title: OpenAI's Greg Brockman gives millions to save eagles Jackie and Shadow's home
content: Greg Brockman and his wife Anna donated five point five million dollars to save shoreline forest.  This significant contribution helped secure ten million dollars for land conservation efforts.  The land, which is home to rare species, will now be protected from development.  Over twenty-five thousand small donors also contributed to the successful fundraising campaign.  Meanwhile, the eagle matriarch Jackie faces an uncertain health prognosis.

title: Supreme Court acquits man after 22 years in jail for wrongful conviction
content: After enduring twenty-two long years of wrongful imprisonment, a man was finally acquitted by the Supreme Court. The injustice stemmed from the trial court's flawed evidence analysis, compounded by the High Court's refusal to entertain his delayed appeal. The Supreme Court emphasized how marginalized communities often find access to justice frustratingly elusive, shedding light on the pressing issues within the judicial system that disproportionately affect the underprivileged.

title: DHS plan hints at higher H1B, L1 visa fees for large companies
content: The US government plans to expand an additional fee for certain visa petitions. This fee currently applies to initial H-1B and L-1 visa grants. The proposed change will extend this charge to petitions for extensions of stay. Companies with over fifty employees and a majority on these visas will be affected. This expansion aims to fund biometric entry-exit systems and other government programs.

title: Jana Nayagan day 14: Thalapathy Vijay film drops 14.3%, India net at Rs 183.35 crore
content: Jana Nayagan's box office collections saw a further slowdown on its fourteenth day. The action drama collected an estimated Rs 1.80 crore in India on Wednesday. Its India net collection has now reached Rs 183.35 crore after fourteen days. Worldwide gross collections for the film have now crossed Rs 306 crore. Tamil Nadu remained the strongest performing market for the film.

title: Aussie snakes have 5 spine zones, necks just 7-12 vertebrae long
content: Recent studies reveal that snake spines are now categorized into five unique anatomical regions. Surprising findings indicate that snakes have a notably short neck, which reflects their ancestral lineage from lizards. Additionally, this research highlights a newly discovered middle thoracic region that has adapted for movement, enhancing their abilities to burrow, swim, and climb. Interestingly, snakes have evolved their skeletons structurally rather than simply after losing their limbs.

title: 54 Asian oak species reviewed: 40 have no backup, 1 may be extinct in the wild
content: Almost three-quarters of Asian oak species find themselves without live representations in botanical gardens, putting countless vulnerable trees in danger of extinction. Agriculture and logging pose significant threats to these essential forest ecosystems. To combat this, immediate fieldwork and seed collection efforts are being organized to safeguard endangered species. The overarching objective of these conservation actions is to create managed collections that can facilitate future reintroduction efforts.

title: Priscilla Chan founded a school in 2016; 10 yrs later, it closed after $125m funding
content: The Primary School, a tuition-free institution, will close in June after a decade of operation. This school provided education, healthcare, and family support to low-income children. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative will not continue funding beyond the upcoming academic year. Academic results remained below state averages, prompting the board's decision. The initiative pledged fifty million dollars to aid the transition for affected students.

title: Centre renews bid for delimitation bill as Rijiju reaches out to Rahul Gandhi
content: The government is pushing its delimitation legislation to increase Lok Sabha seats.  This bill also proposes one-third reservation for women starting in 2029.  Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi rejected the government's outreach for support.  The government may reintroduce the Constitution amendment bill soon.  Discussions continue regarding the Foreign Contributions Regulation Amendment Bill.

title: Government hits out at Pakistan’s malicious propaganda against India
content: In a strong rebuttal, India rejected Pakistan's Youm-e-Istehsal, deeming it as propaganda intended to obscure its own human rights abuses and terrorism connections. The Indian government asserted that the constitutional changes in Jammu and Kashmir fall within its sovereignty, whilst the global community takes note of the human rights oppression occurring in Pakistan-administered regions. Pakistan is called upon to address ongoing bloodshed and relinquish its illegal occupation of Indian territories.

title: How Cristiano Ronaldo overcame poverty and loss to become a football legend
content: Cristiano Ronaldo’s journey is about much more than football. From growing up in poverty and leaving home at 12 to losing his father before achieving global success, every challenge shaped the player he became. His story reminds people that discipline, sacrifice and love for family can help overcome even the hardest moments and turn dreams into reality.

title: How Travis Kelce is transforming lives beyond football in Kansas City
content: Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce supports local children and families. He partnered with Kodiak to provide twenty-five thousand hot meals. Kelce also invested in Operation Breakthrough, a Kansas City nonprofit. His Eighty-Seven & Running Foundation supports youth programs and career exploration. This initiative offers practical skills and a safe space for students.

title: Meet Brock Lesnar's family: Wife Sable, children, parents and siblings
content: Brock Lesnar, the WWE legend, leads a private family life with his wife Sable.  They share two sons, Turk and Duke, who play competitive hockey.  Lesnar also has twins, Mya and Luke, from a previous relationship.  Mya excels in college shot put while Luke wrestles competitively.  Raised on a South Dakota dairy farm, Lesnar credits his parents for his strong work ethic.

title: Supreme Court urges states to decide on raising retirement age of judges by Sept 2
content: The Supreme Court urged states to decide on raising trial court judges' retirement age. This move aims to align their superannuation age with that of High Court judges. States were asked to make this decision by September 2, dismissing financial constraint arguments. The court stated that retaining experienced judges offers financial benefits to the government. High Courts were also requested to support this age enhancement initiative.

title: Trai unveils draft service quality norms for network slicing
content: Indian telecom consumers may soon see network slicing come to life, as the telecom authority has released draft protocols for this groundbreaking technology. These anticipated regulations will enable different internet speeds tailored to various user segments, allowing telecom operators to set unique prices for services like 4G and 5G. This development follows appeals from prominent telecom service providers.

title: Government orders blocking of 7,393 links involved in film pirac
content: The government has directed online intermediaries to block 7,393 links involved in film piracy. This action includes the blocking of 4,996 Telegram channels and 1,263 websites. The information and broadcasting ministry disclosed this directive to the Lok Sabha on Wednesday. This move follows amendments to the Cinematograph Act in 2023. The legal framework against online film piracy has been strengthened by the government.

title: ‘Criminal cases can’t have lifespan of turtle’: SC on activist’s trial delay
content: The Supreme Court voiced apprehension regarding the extended duration of a criminal trial involving a Popular Front of India activist, who could face more than three years behind bars. With 700 witnesses lined up for prosecution, the trial has been severely delayed. The activist is charged with fundraising and supporting alleged terrorism, prompting the court to call for a swift resolution to the drawn-out legal proceedings.

title: 25 India-bound ships in Hormuz; government set to evacuate 13 soon
content: Dozens of Indian and India-bound ships are currently in high-risk maritime zones.  The government has facilitated the safe return of over four thousand stranded Indian seafarers.  Maritime authorities are actively monitoring distress alerts and coordinating rescue operations.  Financial assistance is being provided to the families of deceased seafarers.  The government remains committed to the safety of its maritime workers.

title: 4 tonne piece of SpaceX rocket smashes into moon
content: A hefty four-tonne piece from a SpaceX rocket has made its way to the moon, crashing after an eighteen-month journey in the cosmos. This second stage of the rocket hit the western limb at Einstein crater with considerable force. Currently, lunar satellites are on standby to document the impact and examine the debris. Meanwhile, conversations are underway between NASA and SpaceX to address the risk of future impacts.

title: Rajya Sabha passes by voice vote bill to raise Supreme Court judge strength
content: The Rajya Sabha approved a bill to increase the Supreme Court's judge count. This legislation replaces an ordinance that raised the sanctioned strength to thirty-eight judges. The bill's passage aims to expedite case disposal and enhance judicial efficiency. It will also provide the Chief Justice greater flexibility in forming constitution benches. India anticipates its first woman Chief Justice in the near future.

title: Lok Sabha approves Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill without debate
content: The Lok Sabha recently approved the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, a significant update from an older statute. This new law modernizes the procedures for presenting digital banking records in legal settings. Despite opposition members’ protests and disruptions in the house, the government stood firm, accusing them of hindering religious initiatives and temple projects. Ultimately, the bill passed through a voice vote before the house adjourned.

title: Pradeep Rawat's son Vikramaditya recalls actor's heartbreaking final moments
content: Veteran actor Pradeep Rawat's son, Vikramaditya, broke down as he recalled his father's final moments during the actor's last rites held at Oshiwara Crematorium in Mumbai on Wednesday. Speaking to the media after bidding an emotional farewell to his father, Vikramaditya shared how the family initially believed the actor was suffering from a minor stomach infection before doctors diagnosed him with an aggressive and rare form of blood cancer.

title: Jiya Shankar announces engagement to Kaaran Dhanak; shares dreamy proposal pics
content: Jiya Shankar from Bigg Boss OTT 2 has officially shared the joyous news of her engagement to Kaaran Dhanak. She celebrated this special milestone by posting their heartfelt proposal pictures on social media. The actress expressed her overwhelming love for her fiancé, a US-based entrepreneur, emphasizing their relationship as a captivating adventure akin to her favorite romantic comedy.

title: Trump's immigration crackdown hits US military families; over 50 spouses detained
content: Dozens of parents and spouses of US service members face detention and deportation. This marks a significant shift from prior bipartisan immigration policies for military families. Many are detained during routine immigration status adjustment appointments. The Department of Homeland Security states military service does not exempt violations of immigration laws. These detentions negatively impact military readiness and family stability.

title: Black Sea attack: Merchant Navy officer's family refuses cremation, seeks martyr status
content: Following a brutal attack in the Black Sea, the remains of Merchant Navy chief officer Sagar Gupta were brought back to Kanpur. His family, deeply affected by the loss, has declared they will not conduct any last rites until specific demands are fulfilled, including martyr recognition, financial compensation, and employment for his widow.

title: With all eyes on delimitation & FCRA, monsoon session sinks deeper into deadlock
content: Parliament has hit yet another impasse as the opposition protests continue for the thirteenth day. Despite this, the government succeeded in passing important legislation, including the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill and a bill concerning Supreme Court judges. In an effort to resolve the deadlock, minister Kiren Rijiju met with opposition figures, while Prime Minister Modi focused on discussing strategies with BJP Members of Parliament.

title: Hyderabad CA dies by suicide by inhaling helium over 'gaming losses'
content: In Siddipet, a chartered accountant tragically took his own life, burdened by heavy gambling losses. Employing helium gas, a method learned from online tutorials, he was discovered in a hotel room after the staff notified the authorities. His suicide note revealed the anguish linked to his financial plight, despite family support and efforts to sell his property.

title: Commercial plane takes off as Trump’s helicopter nears airport; FAA investigates

A commercial aircraft took off just as President Trump’s helicopter was nearing Reagan National Airport, leading to a brief loss of separation. Following a tragic midair collision in 2025, stricter regulations have been enforced. The White House assured that the President’s safety was never compromised.
